summary: I read all 45 saved threads in experiments/discussions/*.md in full, with comments, plus all 24 digests. The digests add only the 743929, 744093 and 743006 comments and a notebook list whose best public score is 0.953. I then checked every concrete technique, knob, value or observation against ideas.json (509 ideas), CONTEXT.md, FACTS.md, DECISIONS.md, the knobarms_28sep inventory and the exp85a source. Almost everything from the forum is already adopted, tested or closed in our records: K (743929), float centroids (744093), tight55 and the in-kernel sweep trap (741242, 743222), DET 0.965, secondary weight, Z-flip TTA and candidate threshold (743222), the Ultrack event penalties (740573; APPEARANCE is not an independent axis, I-175), the asymmetric daughter gate (I-080), velocity-projected gap closing (I-174; VELOCITY_WEIGHT is near-inert), cluster-to-centroid (I-134), an N_est count oracle (N_est exists only in train GT), conditional fusion (already x138 low_margin_consensus), test-time adaptation (I-157), a synchrony prior (I-294), mimicking GT noise (I-276), OUTPUT_EDGE_MAX (inert, pre-relink) and a z-shift (I-029, coordinate class). Local verification: VALIDATOR_ENABLE is '0' and LEARNED_BONUS is '1.0' in exp85a, 87a, 89p, 89q, 89r, 89s and exp75, so the 743222 validator trap cannot hit any night or morning file. Only 3 items are not fully tried. (1) MOTION_RELINK_LEARNED_BONUS DOWN, to the code default 0.75. Only the UP arm (2.5, P22, exp29 family) has been read, and it lost. This is the only one feasible by morning, but it is borderline under the no-public-fitting rule and its expected effect is below one display step. (2) An Ultrack-style max_neighbors cap on ILP candidates. There is no knob for it, it needs a patch, and it is not feasible. (3) An annotation-density-aware safe-division gate. It is deferred (I-334) because nothing on the test side can estimate density, so it is not feasible. Recommendation: nothing from the forum justifies displacing a planned night or morning file. The forum's main value now is as evidence for the finals hedge. 743929's own author says his process 'says nothing about the private one'. 743006 (unverified) says private is one embryo. 742064 and 743222 show local and public signs disagreeing on in-sample stacks. All of this supports the already-agreed pair {V_pub, #37/exp75}, not a JT-style near-twin pair.

candidates.idea: Trust the learned association less in the final Hungarian relink: MOTION_RELINK_LEARNED_BONUS 1.0 -> 0.75 (the code's own default; x138 raised it to 1.0), optional deeper arm 0.5.
candidates.source: 743222 (imissher): 'Every change that trusts the learned association more (relink off, lower candidate threshold) failed, while the geometric repair always helped - which fits test being a different embryo.' 742266 (Justin CH123): 'the final edges come from the Hungarian motion relink ... The network probability only enters that cost through the learned bonus, worth at most about 1 um against a median true step of about 1.8 um.' 742064 (Eric): public detectors trained on all 199 videos, so learned probabilities are in-sample-confident. Mechanism: exp85a cost[i,j] = motion + FLOW_RAW_COST*raw - LEARNED_BONUS*prob (exp85a source l.3265); a lower bonus lets flow-predicted geometry decide more pairs.
candidates.how: exp85a (or exp89p for SEC) cell-0 line 14: os.environ["BIOHUB_MOTION_RELINK_LEARNED_BONUS"] = '0.75' (it is not hard-set later; the code default is 0.75 at l.260). Builder: --set BIOHUB_MOTION_RELINK_LEARNED_BONUS=0.75 on the chosen base, then the usual ~30-35 min dummy gate (nodes within +-0.5%, edge churn 0.05-1.5%, fallback_raw/skipped_large_frame 0).
candidates.why_not_public_fit: BORDERLINE. The value 0.75 was not read off the board: it is the tracking code's own default and x138's 1.0 is the author's choice. The direction also has a forum-mechanism basis (743222 and 742064: the learned linker is in-sample on both train embryos). However, our own public read P22 (bonus 2.5 = 0.945, -0.002 vs exp29) already signs the UP side, so moving DOWN is partly the JT two-arm extrapolation the user excluded. It should be admitted only if the user accepts 'revert to the code default' as a non-public choice.
candidates.expected_effect: It only re-wires which relink edges are kept, and relink replaces all ILP edges. Nodes are unchanged except through MIN_TRACK_LEN 6 and the readmit re-run, so the node-count effect is < 0.1%. Size is bounded by the whole relink stage: turning relink off moved 0.947 -> 0.945/0.946 on older stacks, and P22 moved -0.002 at 2.5x. 1.0 -> 0.75 changes the cost by <= 0.25 um per pair, so the expected public |delta| is < 0.001 (probably invisible at 3 decimals). Private sign unknown, with a weak positive prior from the new-embryo mechanism.
candidates.status_in_our_records: Not fully tried. Only the UP arm was read: I-179 / P22 exp41 bonus 2.5 = 0.945 on the exp29 plain-relink family, not x138. knobarms_28sep excluded the knob as 'already probed', and arms_0 has no churn replay for the down arm. I-167 (score unscored relink pairs) is refuted. It is not on the 29 Sep closed list. It would compete with the planned CI/non-CI morning files and the ~3 h GPU; low priority.

candidates.idea: Ultrack-style cap on candidate links per node (max_neighbors 5 within max_distance 10 um) in the ILP candidate graph, instead of x138's probability threshold alone.
candidates.source: 740573 (Le Quang Canh, from royerlab/ultrack_supplementary configs): 'Both zebrafish configs in the supplementary repo use max_distance 10.0 and max_neighbors 5, and the event penalties are small and balanced.' Context: 739516 (Jose Luiz): a nearest-parent candidate graph 'R~9.9um, K<=10' covers ~88% of GT division forks vs ~99.7% of continuations.
candidates.how: No env knob exists. x138 builds candidates from DUAL_SEED_EDGE_THRESHOLD 0.48, which cell 3 hard-sets (I-309). It would need a new patch in predict_video's candidate stage (keep the top-5 by probability per source within 10 um) and a full GPU dummy. There is no build command.
candidates.why_not_public_fit: The value comes from a host-lab reference config, not from the board. Still, there is no lab bed that can sign it (exp60 dumps are post-relink), so any adoption would rest on a public read.
candidates.expected_effect: It prunes ILP candidates in dense regions, which changes the ILP's node selection slightly, and relink then re-wires the edges. The related imissher read (743222: candidate threshold 0.48 -> 0.30, i.e. MORE candidates) was 0.000 on the public board. Expect about 0 and a slight risk to division supply, since daughters are often the 2nd or 3rd candidate.
candidates.status_in_our_records: Untried. No 'max_neighbors' hit in CONTEXT, FACTS, IDEAS or ideas.json. The nearest items are I-309 (DUAL_SEED knobs hard-set) and I-080 (daughter reach). It needs new code plus GPU, has no lab gate and an expected value of about 0, so it is not a 29 Sep item.

candidates.idea: Annotation-density-aware safe-division symmetry gate: relax SAFE_DIV_SISTER_SYMMETRY_TAU only where the embryo's annotation density makes asymmetric forks pay.
candidates.source: 732103 (Ace): 'our real training set turns out to come from only 2 actual embryos, and they differ a lot: annotation sparsity of roughly 1% vs 9%, and division counts of 26 vs 125'. 739018 (hengck23): 'the sparse annotation are not random tracks'. Our own measurement: annotation density per predicted node is 0.79% on 44b6 vs 5.20% on 6bba, and tau is embryo-specific (6bba +0.00434, 44b6 -0.00126).
candidates.how: It needs a per-video density proxy computed at test time, and none exists (N_est is only in train GT). There is no knob, and TAU 0.7 as a plain knob is closed for 29 Sep.
candidates.why_not_public_fit: The idea itself is not public-fit, but it cannot be calibrated without a density proxy. A global tau move is the closed TAU 0.7 rung.
candidates.expected_effect: Lab size is +0.004 on 6bba-like and -0.001 on 44b6-like beds. With a perfect density switch the private gain would be at most ~+0.002, and the node count is essentially unchanged (only forks move).
candidates.status_in_our_records: Deferred after the deadline (I-334, round 13 and round 19): 'no density proxy is available at test time'. A plain tau is closed (I-051, TAU 0.7 on the closed list, I-453 TAU 0.5 refuted).
